featured_reviews.name: vijay wadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Biryani Barbeque Chinese restaurant is a multi cuisine restaurant in Borivali West.
One of the oldest restaurants.
It offers vegetarian and non vegetarian food.
It has good options for non vegetarian Biryani, Chicken tikka, mutton Sikh kabab, tandoori chicken.
It has a good variety of Chinese dishes.
Food quality is good and all the dishes are tasty.
This restaurant has ample seating arrangements on the ground floor and first floor. The ambience is ok.
Service is fast enough.
Generally it is a bit crowded during weekends, but the waiting period is manageable as it has more sitting arrangements on the first floor.
It has valet parking so parking is not an issue.
This restaurant also serves alcohol.
Offers a variety of Indian and imported whisky, Vodka, rum, Gin and liquor. Also has a good choice of beers.
The food prices are ok, but alcohol is on a bit higher side.
Overall it is worth visiting with family and value for money.

featured_reviews.name: Hitesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a satisfying experience at Restro Bar - Biryani Barbeque. The place offers a comfortable dining environment and is well-suited for a relaxed meal with friends or family.

What stands out is that it is one of the few places in Borivali West that serves good quality non-vegetarian food. Given that the area has a significant Gujarati community and is largely dominated by vegetarian options, this restaurant provides a refreshing and much-needed alternative for non-vegetarian diners.

The food was well-prepared, flavourful, and lived up to expectations. The biryani and barbeque items were particularly enjoyable, with balanced spices and good portion sizes. The service was prompt and courteous, contributing positively to the overall experience.

Overall, it is a dependable choice for those looking for good non-vegetarian options in Borivali West, and I would certainly recommend it for a satisfying meal.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A perfect place for seafood lovers, and surprisingly one of the best spots for delicious vegetarian food as well. Located conveniently near Gorai Jetty, this restaurant is a great option for family dinners and weekend outings.
The quality of the food is truly impressive. Every dish tastes fresh, flavorful, and well prepared. Their seafood is excellent, with perfectly balanced spices and authentic taste, while the vegetarian dishes are equally satisfying and full of flavor. It’s rare to find a seafood restaurant that serves such amazing veg food too.
The quantity served is quite generous, making the pricing completely worth it. The rates are very reasonable considering the quality, portion size, and overall dining experience.
The ambiance is pleasant and comfortable, making it a nice place to relax and enjoy a meal with family or friends after visiting Gorai. Service is also good, and the staff is polite and attentive.Overall, a highly recommended restaurant near Gorai Jetty for both seafood and vegetarian food lovers. Great taste, good quantity, reasonable pricing, and a satisfying dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Ankeeta
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Flavorful Dining Experience

Last week, I had the pleasure of visiting Mantra Restaurant, and it turned out to be a fantastic dining experience. Located conveniently, the restaurant is easy to find and has a welcoming vibe from the moment you step in. The ambiance is cozy and well-designed, creating a perfect setting for a relaxing meal. Whether you're dining with family or friends, the atmosphere makes you feel at ease.

Refreshing Start with Mocktails

To begin, we ordered Virgin Mojito and Rose Mojito, and both were super refreshing. The Virgin Mojito had the right balance of mint and lime, while the Rose Mojito had a subtle floral sweetness that made it unique. They set the perfect tone for the meal ahead.

Tasty Starters

For appetizers, we had Tandoori Egg and Hara Bhara Kebab. The Tandoori Egg was a delightful surprise – well-marinated with just the right amount of spice, giving it a smoky flavor. The Hara Bhara Kebab, made with fresh greens and spices, was crispy on the outside and soft inside, making it a great vegetarian option.

Satisfying Main Course

Moving on to the main course, we went for the Pomfret Thali and Chicken Dum Biryani.

The Pomfret Thali was a seafood lover’s dream! The fish was well-cooked, flavorful, and paired perfectly with the side dishes in the thali.

The Chicken Dum Biryani had that signature aroma and taste, with tender chicken pieces and perfectly spiced rice. Every bite was a delight!

Ending on a Sweet Note

For dessert, we had the classic Sizzling Brownie. Served hot with melting chocolate and ice cream, it was the perfect way to end the meal. Rich, chocolatey, and satisfying!

Service & Hospitality

The staff was incredibly nice and welcoming. Their service was smooth and effortless, making sure we had everything we needed. The overall experience was easygoing and hassle-free, adding to the enjoyment of the meal.

Final Thoughts

Mantra Restaurant truly lives up to expectations with its great food, lovely ambiance, and excellent service. Whether you’re craving refreshing mocktails, flavorful starters, or a hearty main course, this place has something for everyone. A must-visit for anyone who enjoys good food in a comfortable setting!

Would I go back? Absolutely!

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pangat is one of those places you walk into with high expectations, especially given its reputation for Malvani thalis and coastal favourites. Having been regular patrons for many years, this place has held a certain nostalgic charm for us, which made our recent visits all the more noticeable in contrast.
We sampled a fairly elaborate spread, including their Bombil Thali, Surmai Thali, Prawns Thali, Mandeli fry, along with add ons like the much talked about Crab Lollypop, Bheja Masala, Kalva Sukka, Chicken Potli Kebab, and also revisited dishes we have enjoyed in the past like the keema pattice, bombil fry, and mutton masala.
While the menu continues to promise a seafood lover’s delight, the overall experience, unfortunately, felt average this time around. The Bombil and Surmai fry had the expected crispness, but lacked that depth of flavour and freshness that truly elevates coastal cuisine. The curries across thalis felt somewhat one dimensional, missing the robust, layered Malvani masala profile one associates with Pangat. Even the basics like chapatis and bhakris, which form the backbone of such meals, could be softer, fresher, and more refined.
On a more specific note, the tisrya masala (dry) felt quite chewy, almost rubbery in texture, taking away from what is otherwise a delightful dish when done right. The solkadhi, too, seemed to miss that refreshing kokam forward tang we have experienced here earlier and elsewhere.
That said, what truly stood out and deserves full credit was the service and hospitality. The staff handled everything with genuine warmth, attentiveness, and honesty. From guiding through the menu to ensuring timely service, their effort and intent were clearly heartfelt, and it did make a meaningful difference to the overall dining experience.
Pangat certainly has the foundation of a great dining destination, and perhaps it is just a matter of revisiting the fundamentals. With a bit more attention to core elements like breads, curries, and flavour balance, it has every potential to regain the consistency and charm it was once known for.
For now, a place that still offers variety, but one we hope will soon rediscover the flavours that made it special for us over the years.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried out Borivali Biryani Centre recently and honestly – if you’re a biryani lover, this place should be on your list!

We had their Chicken Tikka Dum Biryani and it was amazing. The flavors were spot on – smoky, spicy, and super satisfying. We also tried the Jahangir Tikka, and it was perfectly grilled with just the right amount of spice. Really juicy and flavorful – definitely worth a try.

To sip on, we ordered a mojito, which was alright – refreshing but nothing extraordinary.

Now here’s the thing – the biryanis here steal the show. If you’re visiting, go for the biryanis. That’s where they truly shine. Other stuff’s okay, but nothing comes close to their signature biryani.

A heads-up though: the place gets really crowded. There’s usually a long queue outside, so if you’re planning a visit, try to go early or see if you can reserve a table. We had to call the staff multiple times just to place an order, and while they were polite, they seemed short-staffed for the kind of crowd they handle.

On the plus side, the ambiance is nice and fresh, and the restaurant has a clean, cozy vibe.

Final verdict:

Come for the biryani. Be patient with the service. Totally worth it if you’re craving something flavorful and filling. Would recommend, just plan your timing!

If you’re craving tasty North Indian food with great quality and service, Kebab Kitchen is definitely worth trying! 🔥🍽️
